name: Sotto Voce
geological_features: Irregularly shaped body suggesting it is a captured object rather than a formed planetesimal
Surface of fused exotic minerals with a glassy, mirror-like finish in places
Deep fissures exposing interior strata of unknown crystalline material
specific_features: Exotic matter deposits that produce localized gravitational anomalies, with objects falling at inconsistent rates across the surface
A persistent low-energy emission in a frequency band that does not correspond to any known natural process
Surface material that resists spectral analysis, returning readings inconsistent with known elements
resources: Exotic matter with gravitational manipulation properties
Unclassified crystalline material of potential technological significance
Research value rated as incalculable by three independent survey teams
description: Sotto Voce is a tiny, irregularly shaped body drifting in the outer reaches of its star system, barely large enough to be called a planetoid. Its surface is a patchwork of glassy, mirror-smooth exotic minerals and rough fissures exposing crystalline strata that do not match any known geological process. At 680 kilometers across, it has almost no gravity — yet instruments detect gravitational anomalies across its surface that suggest something inside is bending spacetime in ways that should not be possible for an object of this mass.

The planetoid emits a faint, continuous signal in a frequency band that sits between radio and microwave — too structured to be natural thermal emission, too faint and invariant to be a beacon. Researchers have taken to calling it the whisper, and the planetoid's name reflects this: sotto voce, spoken softly, barely there. The signal does not respond to attempts at communication and does not change regardless of what is done to the surface.

Three independent survey teams have declared Sotto Voce's research value incalculable, and none have been able to explain what it is. The exotic matter in its fissures produces gravitational effects that violate standard models — objects dropped at different points on the surface fall at measurably different rates, and in one documented case, a dropped tool rose instead of fell before drifting laterally and settling. The material resists spectral analysis, returning readings that correspond to no known element or compound.

Sotto Voce has been placed under restricted access, but the restriction is enforced more by its remoteness than by any patrol presence. The few researchers permitted on-site work in shifts, reporting unusual psychological effects including a persistent sense of being observed and difficulty forming new memories while on the surface. Whether these effects are caused by the exotic matter, the gravitational anomalies, or simple isolation remains undetermined. What is certain is that Sotto Voce is not a natural object — and whatever made it is nowhere to be found.
